numerical_results.method: Gillespie Kinetic Monte Carlo with active-edge list optimization
numerical_results.key_finding: All four scenarios reach near-heat-death (Q < 0.03). Chi never approaches Frechet bound. Chi-braking is NOT observed at the microscopic single-trajectory level.

claims.statement: The core R1/R2 prediction (chi-braking prevents heat death) is FALSIFIED at the microscopic single-trajectory level for the tested parameter ranges
claims.support: §2.3-2.4: 170 independent realizations across 4 scenarios, all reaching Q < 0.03

claims.statement: Chi-braking is a weakly emergent (N->infinity limit) phenomenon, not a microscopic deterministic barrier
claims.support: §3.1: micro-macro gap analysis, §3.2: thermodynamic analogy, §3.3: conditions for braking to manifest
claims.testable: P-R3-2: scaling analysis with increasing L

claims.statement: For random independent ICs, Q(t) follows logistic decay dQ/dt = -gamma0 * Q * (1-Q) rather than self-limiting braking
claims.support: §2.3: Q(t) curves from all four scenarios
claims.testable: Fit logistic parameters to Q(t) data

claims.statement: Chi_max scales as ~1/sqrt(N) (finite-size fluctuation) rather than approaching Frechet bound
claims.support: §3.1.2: finite-size analysis, scenario 1 vs 2 chi_max ratio consistent with scaling
claims.confidence: medium (predictive, needs verification at multiple L)

claims.statement: Chi-braking requires at least one of: (a) prepared high-chi IC, (b) competing reverse channel, or (c) true N->infinity limit
claims.support: §3.3: three necessary conditions derived from simulation analysis

layer_1.name: Micro-macro gap: why chi-braking vanishes in single trajectories
layer_1.key_insight: Macroscopic rate equations describe ensemble expectations, not individual trajectories. Single configurations have 0/1 indicator functions, not smooth probabilities. Chi feedback requires ensemble-level averaging.
layer_1.standing: solid (explains the discrepancy between R1/R2 theory and R3 simulation)

layer_2.name: Thermodynamic analogy: chi-braking as weak second law
layer_2.key_insight: Unlike standard second law (backed by Liouville theorem + ergodicity), chi-braking lacks both a micro-conserved quantity and an invariant measure. It is a weak emergent constraint, not a strong deterministic law.
layer_2.math_provided: partial (large deviation formulation, rate function estimate)

layer_3.name: Conditions for chi-braking to actually manifest
layer_3.key_insight: Three necessary conditions identified: high-chi IC, competing reverse channel, or N->infinity. Pure dissipative DGF with random IC cannot exhibit braking.

new_predictions.statement: Q(t) follows logistic decay for random ICs
Goldilocks window of initial chi_0 for braking to manifest
Competing reverse channel enables non-trivial steady state with chi > 0
Intermittent bursts require reverse channel (pure dissipative DGF has no intermittency)
new_predictions.testability: high (burst statistics from existing S1-S4 data)

failed_jumps.attempt: Direct numerical integration of BBGKY second-order closure ODEs
failed_jumps.reason_abandoned: 4500 coupled stiff ODEs; adaptive step sizes collapse to 1e-12 near Frechet boundary. Numerically intractable.
failed_jumps.lesson: BBGKY closure is analytically useful but numerically impractical — KMC is the right tool for verification.

self_attacks.attack: Simulation results prove chi-braking theory is false
self_attacks.response: Partially conceded for microscopic level. Theory is correct at macroscopic (rate equation) level but does not translate to single-trajectory predictions. Scope of theory narrowed.

self_attacks.attack: 30x30 grid too small — critical behavior might emerge at larger L
self_attacks.response: Scaling analysis suggests chi_max DECREASES with L (1/sqrt(N)), not increases. Larger systems make braking HARDER, not easier. Counter-intuitive but consistent with central limit theorem.
self_attacks.severity: medium (addressed by scaling argument, needs verification)

self_attacks.attack: Chi-dependent rate simulation (S4) failed due to poor chi estimation, not due to absence of braking
self_attacks.response: Conceded. Better estimation requires larger windows -> computationally infeasible per-step. This is a practical limitation, not a refutation of chi-dependent braking in principle.
